gloss: flesh and blood; living body; mortal body

definitions.gloss: flesh and blood; living body; mortal body
definitions.explanation: The actual physical body of a living human being, as opposed to something mechanical, digital, or supernatural.

examples.japanese: {生身|なまみ}の{人間|にんげん}には{限界|げんかい}がある。
ロボットではなく、{生身|なまみ}の{人|ひと}と{話|はな}したい。
examples.english: I want to talk to a real person, not a robot.

examples.japanese: {生身|なまみ}の{体|からだ}で{宇宙|うちゅう}に{出|で}ることはできない。
examples.english: You can't go out into space with an unprotected human body.

notes:
A compound of {生|なま} (raw, living) and {身|み} (body). Emphasizes the vulnerability and reality of the physical human body.

USAGE:
Almost always appears in the phrase {生身|なまみ}の{人間|にんげん} (a flesh-and-blood human) or {生身|なまみ}の{体|からだ} (a mortal body). Used when contrasting real people with machines, virtual beings, or superhuman entities. Carries a nuance of human vulnerability and physicality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生身|なまみ}の{人間|にんげん} — a real, flesh-and-blood human
- {生身|なまみ}の{体|からだ} — a mortal/physical body
- {生身|なまみ}で — with one's bare body; unprotected

RELATED TERMS:
- {肉体|にくたい} — physical body; the body as opposed to the mind or spirit
- {素手|すで} — bare hands; without tools or weapons
- {本人|ほんにん} — the person themselves; in person
